div.div: no matter how powerful your CPUs are, your node's ability to move data in and out is strictly capped by the virtual hardware it runs on.

div.div: MTU: 9001 (Jumbo Frames) supported; set via AWS_VPC_ENI_MTU in the VPC CNI.

div.div: The difference between your VPC's 9001 MTU and your container's 1500 MTU is a classic "mismatch" that determines how data is chopped up before it travels across the network.

div.div: VPC Default: 9001 Bytes (The "Jumbo Frame"): This only works inside the AWS network (VPC-to-VPC or VPC-to-DirectConnect).

path.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

div.div: Most Docker containers and Kubernetes Pods default to 1500 bytes. This is the standard size for the entire public Internet (Ethernet standard)

rect.style: fill: light-dark(#ffffff, var(--ge-dark-color, #121212)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 458px; height: 1px; padding-top: 380px; margin-left: 1251px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: For High-Performance AI/ML: Some engineers tune their CNI (like Calico or the AWS VPC CNI) to use an MTU of 8951 or 9001 for pod-to-pod traffic to eke out every bit of performance. However, if that pod ever tries to talk to the Internet without a translator, the connection will likely break.
